import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 689
*References:*
* [erdosproblems.com/689](https://www.erdosproblems.com/689)
* [Ben Green's Open Problem 45](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.45)
-/

namespace Erdos689

/--
Let `n` be sufficiently large. Is there some choice of congruence class `a_p` for all primes
`2 ≤ p ≤ n` such that every integer in `[1,n]` satisfies at least two of the congruences
`≡ a_p (mod p)`?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_689 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᶠ n in .atTop, ∃ a : ℕ → ℕ, ∀ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n,
      2 ≤ (Finset.Icc 1 n |>.filter fun p => p.Prime ∧ a p ≡ m [MOD p]).card := by
  sorry

end Erdos689

reformulations.difference: The residue classes are represented by an unrestricted total function `a : ℕ → ℕ`, rather than a family indexed only by eligible primes with representatives bounded by their moduli.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For each n, restrict a to primes p ≤ n and replace a p by a p % p. Primality makes p positive, so this gives a representative in Fin p without changing any congruences. Conversely, extend a prime-indexed family by assigning 0 at irrelevant indices. The filtered cardinality is at least two exactly when two distinct eligible primes cover m; primality also supplies the lower bound p ≥ 2 despite the interval starting at 1. In /workspace/review/equivalence.lean I proved the entire RHS equivalent to an explicit cutoff followed by existence of such canonical prime-indexed residue families, without using sorry axioms.

review.notes: The sole theorem matches the exact twofold-covering question on the Erdős site, which still records it as OPEN. Green's Problem 45 asks for tenfold coverage, but its comments explicitly pose the unresolved twofold case. Small-input computations and proofs confirm that n=0 is vacuous and n=1,2 fail for every choice; these initial cases are harmless under eventual quantification. Both scratch files compile successfully, and the reviewed file was not modified.
